title: Capitulation
teaches: The capitulation as we trade it: a straight-down burst in a liquid stock or index, ending in a flush day whose low sits 2 ATR or more under the prior close on at least twice the usual volume, 15% or more off the 10-session high. We never buy the falling price or the flush close. We buy the undercut and reclaim of the flush low within 3 sessions, stop a few cents under the low of the day we bought, take a third at 3R and 5R, and accept the stop as the cost of being early.

steps: ALB on 2010-05-06, the flash-crash session. The low is 17.2% under the 10-day high close and 3.94 ATR under the prior close.
Three lower closes, then a spike low. We do not buy the flush close. We wait for the turn.

The stock traded 41% under the buy. The crash had one more leg. The stop kept the loss small.

questions.q: What marks the flush day in a capitulation?
choices: A low 2+ ATR under the prior close
A small gap up on very light volume
A close at a fresh 52-week high
A tight inside day on thin volume
questions.answer: A low 2+ ATR under the prior close
questions.why: A low 2 ATR or more under the prior close. The flush day is wide and fast, with the low far under yesterday's close.
questions.lesson_line: The flush day is a 2 ATR drop, not a drift.

wrong.A small gap up on very light volume: A capitulation is a fast drop on heavy volume, not a quiet gap up.
wrong.A close at a fresh 52-week high: A flush is the opposite of a new high.
wrong.A tight inside day on thin volume: A tight inside day is quiet. The flush is wide.

questions.q: In a capitulation we buy the flush-day close.
questions.why: False. We do not buy the falling price or the flush close. Nearly half of flush closes are undercut the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Do not buy the falling price or the flush close.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The daily trigger is the undercut and ___ of the flush low.
questions.why: Reclaim. A session trades under the flush low and then back above it, and the buy is the reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: Undercut, then reclaim. The reclaim is the buy.

questions.q: What does heavy volume at the lows say, by Kell?
choices: Nothing; volume is just noise here
The trend is quietly healthy again
questions.why: Fear has set in and traders are capitulating. The Wyckoff school describes the same thing as heavy, panicky selling near a bottom.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy volume at the lows is panic, not control.

wrong.Buyers have taken full control: Heavy volume at the lows shows panic selling, not control by buyers.
wrong.Nothing; volume is just noise here: Volume is the main tell of a panic.
wrong.The trend is quietly healthy again: A panic is the opposite of a quiet, healthy trend.

questions.q: A decline on falling volume qualifies as a capitulation.
questions.why: False. A decline on falling volume does not qualify. Wyckoff notes a downtrend can also end without climactic action.
questions.lesson_line: Falling volume is a fade, not a capitulation.

questions.q: How much volume do we want on the flush day?
choices: Any volume will do on a big drop
questions.why: At least 2 times the 50-day average. A panic shows up as heavy volume, ideally the highest of the decline or the year.
questions.lesson_line: A flush needs at least twice the usual volume.

wrong.Half of the 50-day average volume: A panic on half the usual volume is not a panic.
wrong.About the 50-day average volume: Ordinary volume does not mark a flush. We want at least 2 times.
wrong.Any volume will do on a big drop: Volume is one of the gates. Falling volume does not qualify.

questions.q: Tap the number for a stock, not a 3x ETF.
questions.sentence: A stock must fall at least ___ from its highest close of the last 10 sessions.
questions.why: 15%. A stock needs a fall of at least 15% from its highest close of the last 10 sessions. A 3x ETF needs 30%.
questions.lesson_line: Stocks need 15% off the 10-session high. 3x ETFs need 30%.

questions.q: How far under its 50-day should an index close in a flush?
questions.why: At least 3 ATR. Bracco finds intermediate corrections bottom around 3 ATR under the 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: An index flush closes 3 ATR or more under its 50-day.

wrong.At least 1 ATR: One ATR under the 50-day is a pullback, not a flush.
wrong.At least 10 ATR: Ten ATR is far beyond a flush.
wrong.Right at the 50-day: At the 50-day there is no stretch at all.

questions.q: A capitulation flush closes below the 5-day, the 9 EMA and the 20 EMA.
questions.why: True. Price sits below the 5-day SMA, the 9 EMA and the 20 EMA when the flush ends.
questions.lesson_line: The flush leaves price under the 5-day, 9 EMA and 20 EMA.

questions.q: How many lower closes should come before the flush day?
questions.why: At least 2. A capitulation is not a one-day shock out of nowhere. It comes after the stock has already been falling.
questions.lesson_line: Two or more lower closes come before the flush.

wrong.None; a one-day shock counts: A one-day shock out of nowhere is not the setup.
wrong.At least 10: The burst is a few days, not ten.
wrong.Exactly 1: One lower close is not enough. We want at least 2.

questions.q: A close below the lower Bollinger band is a buy signal.
questions.why: False. A close below the lower band is evidence only, never the trigger. Bollinger himself says it is not a buy signal.
questions.lesson_line: A band close is evidence. The reclaim is the trigger.

questions.q: What is the taught daily trigger for a capitulation?
choices: Undercut the flush low, reclaim it
Buy right at the flush day's close
Buy a break of the flush-day high
Buy the first green day after it
questions.answer: Undercut the flush low, reclaim it
questions.why: Undercut the flush low, then reclaim it. Within 3 sessions of the flush a session trades under the low and back above it.
questions.lesson_line: Buy the reclaim of the flush low, within 3 sessions.

wrong.Buy right at the flush day's close: Nearly half of flush closes are undercut the next day.
wrong.Buy a break of the flush-day high: That puts the stop far under the entry. The reclaim keeps it close.
wrong.Buy the first green day after it: A green day is not a trigger. The reclaim of the flush low is.

questions.q: A capitulation read needs a stock at $10 or more that trades $20 million a day.
questions.why: True. Price at least $10 and at least $20 million traded a day. Thinner stocks are skipped.
questions.lesson_line: Price $10 or more, $20 million a day or more.

questions.q: Which is a level that matters under a flush?
choices: A prior high or round number
questions.answer: A prior high or round number
questions.why: A prior high or a round number. The flush works best into a level, such as a prior all-time high, a round number or the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A flush into a real level is a better flush.

wrong.Yesterday's open, by the high: That is not a level the market has respected.
wrong.Yesterday's close, above it: Yesterday's close is where the flush started, not a level under it.
wrong.A 3-day average of the closes: A short average is above a flush. It is not support under it.

questions.q: Prior close 80.00, ATR 2.50, today's low 74.60. How many ATR under the prior close is the low?
questions.why: 2.16 ATR. (80.00 - 74.60) / 2.50. That clears the 2 ATR bar for a flush day.
questions.lesson_line: Drop in dollars, divided by the ATR.

questions.q: The highest close of the last 10 sessions was 120.00 and the flush low is 100.00. How far is the drop, in percent?
questions.why: 16.7%. (120.00 - 100.00) / 120.00. A stock needs at least 15%, so this one clears the stretch.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the drop from the 10-session high close.

questions.q: QQQ's 50-day is 500 and its ATR is 8. It closes at 472. How many ATR under the 50-day is it?
questions.why: 3.5 ATR. (500 - 472) / 8. An index flush wants at least 3 ATR under the 50-day, so this one qualifies.
questions.lesson_line: Distance under the 50-day, divided by the ATR.

questions.q: A Wyckoff trader buys right at the selling climax.
questions.why: False. The Wyckoff trader buys a successful test, such as a spring. The CMT says a climax must be tested first.
questions.lesson_line: Even the Wyckoff school waits for the test.

questions.q: Kell says trading the daily Reversal Extension at once is often best avoided.
questions.why: True. Kell says trading the daily Reversal Extension is often best avoided. We do not buy the falling price either.
questions.lesson_line: The early buy is the risky buy.

questions.q: Bracco notes that notable capitulations and turns have occurred on a Monday.
questions.why: True. Bracco writes that through his studies notable capitulations and turns have occurred on a Monday.
questions.lesson_line: Bracco has seen notable turns on Mondays, after several down days.

questions.q: A capitulation needs an RS rating of 80 or more.
questions.why: False. Mean-reversion and parabolic trades are exempt from the leader rule. Bracco still prefers leaders.
questions.lesson_line: No RS requirement here, though leaders are preferred.

questions.q: Buy the close, or wait?
choices: Wait for the undercut and reclaim
Buy the close; it is record volume
Buy half now and half later
Buy tomorrow's open, whatever it is
questions.story: The flush day closes at its low on record volume, 4 ATR under yesterday's close. It looks like the bottom.
questions.answer: Wait for the undercut and reclaim
questions.why: Wait. We do not buy the flush close. Nearly half of flush closes are undercut the next day, so the turn comes first.
questions.lesson_line: Buy the turn, not the knife.

wrong.Buy the close; it is record volume: Record volume shows the panic. It does not show the low is in.
wrong.Buy half now and half later: Half a knife is still a knife. We buy once, at the reclaim.
wrong.Buy tomorrow's open, whatever it is: A blind open is not a trigger. The reclaim of the flush low is.

questions.q: Where do you buy?
choices: At 38.31, the new low of the day
At the close of the flush day
On a break of the flush high
questions.story: The flush low is 38.40. The next day price trades down to 38.31, then climbs back above 38.40.
questions.why: On the reclaim back above 38.40, the flush low. The undercut to 38.31 sets the stop, a few cents under it.
questions.lesson_line: Undercut the flush low, then buy the reclaim.

wrong.At 38.31, the new low of the day: You cannot know the low is in until price reclaims. The reclaim is the buy.
wrong.At the close of the flush day: That is the knife. Nearly half of flush closes are undercut.
wrong.On a break of the flush high: That entry puts the stop far away. The reclaim keeps it near.

questions.q: Reclaim at 38.49, undercut low 38.31, stop at 38.26. How far is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 0.6%. (38.49 - 38.26) / 38.49. A stop a few cents under the undercut low is very tight.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits a few cents under the undercut low.

questions.q: Entry 38.49, stop 38.26. Where is 5R, where we sell the second third?
questions.why: 39.64. One R is 38.49 minus 38.26. Five of those above the entry is 39.64, where we sell the second third.
questions.lesson_line: 5R is five risk units above the entry.

questions.q: Is this a panic flush?
choices: No; it is an earnings reaction
Yes; a 20% drop is a flush
No; it fell too slowly to count
questions.story: A leader drops 20% in two days right after it reports earnings.
questions.answer: No; it is an earnings reaction
questions.why: No. An earnings reaction is not a panic flush, so we keep the two apart. Of 346 scan hits above the 200-day, 150 had a report inside the window.
questions.lesson_line: Keep earnings reactions apart from panic flushes.

wrong.Yes; a 20% drop is a flush: The size is not the test. A report inside the window sets it apart.
wrong.Yes; earnings cause every flush: An earnings reaction is its own event. We keep the two apart.
wrong.No; it fell too slowly to count: Two days is fast. The report is what sets it apart.

questions.q: Buy the reclaim?
choices: No; the report is 2 sessions away
Yes; the reclaim is the trigger
Yes, but at half size to be safe
No; reports only matter for shorts
questions.story: The reclaim triggers two sessions before the company reports earnings.
questions.answer: No; the report is 2 sessions away
questions.why: No. We take no new buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report, even on a clean trigger.
questions.lesson_line: A clean trigger still waits out the report.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is the trigger: The trigger does not override the report window.
wrong.Yes, but at half size to be safe: Smaller size does not remove the report gap risk. The rule is no new buy.
wrong.No; reports only matter for shorts: The report window applies to new buys.

questions.q: Buy now?
choices: Yes; the setup is still intact
Yes, with a wider stop to fit it
Yes, at half size to cut the risk
questions.story: The trigger price is 50.00. You look late and the stock trades at 52.40.
questions.why: No. 52.40 is 4.8% above 50.00, past the 4% limit. We never buy more than 4% above the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the trigger, it is a pass.

wrong.Yes; the setup is still intact: An intact setup still has a chase limit. No buy more than 4% above the trigger.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop to fit it: Chasing already stretches the distance to the stop and shrinks the size. The rule is no buy past 4%.
wrong.Yes, at half size to cut the risk: Half size does not repair a late entry. The limit is 4%.

questions.q: Is that a trigger?
choices: No; it is evidence, not a trigger
Yes; a close outside is the trigger
No; bands never matter at all
questions.story: The stock closes under the lower Bollinger band for the second day in a row. A friend calls it a buy signal.
questions.answer: No; it is evidence, not a trigger
questions.why: No. A close under the lower band is evidence only. Bollinger says closes outside the bands are initially continuation signals.
questions.lesson_line: A stretched close is not a turn.

wrong.Yes; a close outside is the trigger: A band tag is not in itself a buy signal.
wrong.Yes, after three closes outside: More closes outside the band can mean the trend is walking down it.
wrong.No; bands never matter at all: They help as evidence of a stretch. They are just not the trigger.

questions.q: What does that tell you?
choices: An early warning; the stop rules
A buy signal; add more on the dip
The stop should move down a bit
questions.story: You bought the reclaim. The first bounce day closes in the lower third of its range.
questions.answer: An early warning; the stop rules
questions.why: An early warning. A bounce that stalls on day one and closes in its lower third is weak, but the stop is still the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A weak first bounce is a warning. Keep the stop.

wrong.A buy signal; add more on the dip: We never average down. It is full size at one price.
wrong.Nothing; one candle means little: It is the early warning. Watch the stop closely.
wrong.The stop should move down a bit: The stop only moves up, never down.

questions.q: Is this a capitulation?
choices: No; a slow mark down, not a burst
Yes; it passes all of the numbers
Yes; any drop over 2 ATR counts
No; the volume is far too high
questions.story: A stock slides over three weeks in a controlled mark down. Then it drops 2.61 ATR on 2.02x volume, 15.3% off its 10-day high.
questions.answer: No; a slow mark down, not a burst
questions.why: No. A slow grind or a controlled mark down is not a capitulation, even when the last day's numbers look right.
questions.lesson_line: Look left. A slow grind is not a burst.

wrong.Yes; it passes all of the numbers: The day's numbers pass. The three weeks before it were a controlled mark down.
wrong.Yes; any drop over 2 ATR counts: The drop must end a burst, not a slow grind.
wrong.No; the volume is far too high: 2.02x clears the 2x bar. Heavy volume is wanted.

questions.q: Capitulation, or not?
choices: Not a setup; no lower closes first
Yes; a 20% one-day drop is a flush
Yes; heavy volume is enough alone
Yes, but only if it is a Monday
questions.story: A stock sits flat for a week. Then it falls 20% in a single session on heavy volume.
questions.answer: Not a setup; no lower closes first
questions.why: Not a setup. A one-day shock out of nowhere has no lower closes before it. We want at least 2.
questions.lesson_line: A shock with no run-up is not a burst.

wrong.Yes; a 20% one-day drop is a flush: The size is not enough. It needs a run of lower closes first.
wrong.Yes; heavy volume is enough alone: Volume is one gate, not the only one.
wrong.Yes, but only if it is a Monday: The weekday does not fix a missing burst.

questions.q: Does the volume qualify?
choices: No; the flush needs 2 times the average
Yes; three down days is enough
questions.story: A leader is down three days in a row. The flush day trades only 1.3 times its 50-day average volume.
questions.answer: No; the flush needs 2 times the average
questions.why: No. Flush-day volume needs to be at least 2 times the 50-day average, and ideally the highest of the decline.
questions.lesson_line: Modest volume is a pullback, not a panic.

wrong.Yes; volume is up: Up a little is not a panic. The bar is 2 times.
wrong.Yes; three down days is enough: Down days are one gate. Volume is another.

questions.q: Does it pass?
choices: No; volume is just under the 2x bar
Yes; 1.96 rounds up to the 2x bar
Yes; volume is optional on a big ATR
No; the ATR is too small to count
questions.story: A flush day: 2.13 ATR, 15.2% off the 10-day high, above the 200-day. Volume is 1.96 times the 50-day average.
questions.answer: No; volume is just under the 2x bar
questions.why: No. The whole shape is there, but volume is 1.96 times the average and the bar is 2 times. A rule is a line.
questions.lesson_line: A near miss is still a miss.

wrong.Yes; 1.96 rounds up to the 2x bar: The test is the number, not a rounding. 1.96 is under 2.
wrong.Yes; volume is optional on a big ATR: Volume is a gate. A big ATR does not stand in for it.

questions.q: Which rule stops the buy?
choices: The 200-day rule, no longs under it
The earnings rule before a report
The 4% chase limit above the trigger
The volume rule: at least 2 times
questions.story: The reclaim closes 15.9% under the 200-day. The stock slid for two months, then dropped 2.19 ATR on 3.48x volume.
questions.answer: The 200-day rule, no longs under it
questions.why: The 200-day rule. We take no longs below the 200-day unless it is a parabolic long, and a two-month slide is not a burst.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, a slow slide is a watch, not a buy.

wrong.The 4% chase limit above the trigger: Nothing here is above the trigger.

questions.q: Bulkowski found that nearly half of one-day collapses make a lower low the next day.
questions.why: True. Forty-six percent make a lower low the next day. Buying the first close is early, which is why we wait for the reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: Nearly half make a lower low the next day.

questions.q: After a big one-day drop, Bulkowski's average bounce is how big, and how long?
questions.why: 28% over 23 days. Then price resumes declining, averaging 30% in 49 days. Bracco calls these 1-3 day trades.
questions.lesson_line: The bounce is a trade, not a new trend.

wrong.5% over 2 days: His average bounce is 28% and takes 23 days.
wrong.60% over 6 months: His average bounce is 28% and takes 23 days.
wrong.No bounce at all: There is a bounce. It just does not last.

questions.q: In Bulkowski's own trades, what share of buys in stage 4, the downtrend, made money?
questions.why: 24.41%. Only about a quarter of stage 4 buys made money, against 69.3% of stage 1 buys. It fits our rule against longs under the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Buying a downtrend loses most of the time.

wrong.69.3%: That is the share of stage 1 buys that made money.

questions.q: Buy the huge volume now?
choices: Wait; the low broke the next day
Buy now; the volume is huge
questions.story: A stock falls 77% in 3 days on 7.0x volume. Bracco says a long may set up in the next 1-2 weeks.
questions.answer: Wait; the low broke the next day
questions.why: Wait. Bracco said 1-2 weeks, and the low broke the next day. The stock traded 25% under it within 5 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Even a 77% fall can fall further. Wait for the turn.

wrong.Buy now; the volume is huge: Huge volume showed the panic. It did not show the low.
wrong.Buy half now: Half a knife is still a knife.
wrong.Buy the next open: The next day broke the low.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Hold; it should bounce back soon
questions.story: You bought at 20.00 with a stop at 19.80. The stock gaps down and the first 30-minute low is 19.30.
questions.why: Out. On a gap through the stop the first 30-minute low is the new stop, and a loss past 2R means get out.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop caps at 2R. Past that, leave.

wrong.Hold; it should bounce back soon: The stop is the exit. Hope is not a plan.
wrong.Move the stop down to 19.00: The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take the trims right at the open
Wait for a pullback to the 20 EMA
Hold everything and let it run
Add more at 26.00 on the gap
questions.story: You bought at 22.13 with a stop at 21.72. 5R is 24.18. The next day opens at 26.00.
questions.answer: Take the trims right at the open
questions.why: Take the trims at the open. A stock that opens above a trim level is sold there. MP then closed at 21.94, through its stop.
questions.lesson_line: If it opens past a trim level, sell the trim at the open.

wrong.Wait for a pullback to the 20 EMA: A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
wrong.Hold everything and let it run: Holding it all gave back the gain. MP closed through its stop.
wrong.Add more at 26.00 on the gap: We never add after a gap up or when down. One price, one stop.

questions.q: What do we sell at 3R and again at 5R?
choices: A third of the shares each time
Half of the position each time
All of it at 3R and stay flat
questions.answer: A third of the shares each time
questions.why: A third each time. A third at 3R, another third at 5R, then we trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest.

wrong.Half of the position each time: The rule is a third at each level.
wrong.All of it at 3R and stay flat: We take a third at 3R and keep the rest working.
wrong.Nothing until the 10-day breaks: The trims come first, at 3R and 5R.

questions.q: We move the stop to breakeven at 2R because these bounces fade.
questions.why: True. For a capitulation the stop goes to breakeven at 2R, the low end of the 2R to 5R window.
questions.lesson_line: These bounces fade, so breakeven comes early.

questions.q: If a capitulation buy dips toward the stop, add to average down.
questions.why: False. Never average down. It is the full size at one price with one stop, and Bracco says he never adds when down.
questions.lesson_line: Never average down. One price, one stop.

questions.q: How do we trail the last third?
questions.why: Under each higher daily low until price closes back above the 10-day. After that we sell on a close below the 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the lows, then the 10-day.

wrong.The 200-day: The 200-day is far too slow for a bounce trade.
wrong.A fixed 10% stop: A fixed stop does not follow the bounce.

questions.q: Bracco treats these as short lived trades, not held longer than 1-3 days.
questions.why: True. He writes that these are short lived trades, not meant to be held longer than 1-3 days.
questions.lesson_line: Treat the bounce as a short trade, not a new trend.

questions.q: Which backdrop helps a market-wide flush?
choices: A VIX near 30 and washed-out breadth
questions.answer: A VIX near 30 and washed-out breadth
questions.why: A VIX near 30 and washed-out breadth. Fear is high and rising fast, and T2108 sits near or under 15% to 20%.
questions.lesson_line: A real flush has fear and washed-out breadth behind it.

wrong.A VIX near 10 and calm: A calm market has no fear behind it.
wrong.Breadth near its highs: Strong breadth is the opposite of a washout.
wrong.A slow drift lower: A slow, controlled mark down is not a capitulation.

questions.q: Bracco says big support areas tend to be what, before they are reclaimed?
questions.why: Undercut first. Markets typically undercut big support areas before reclaiming them, if they do.
questions.lesson_line: Support is usually undercut before it is reclaimed.

wrong.Gapped over at once: He says markets typically undercut support first.
wrong.Left alone: He says markets typically undercut support first.
wrong.Rallied 20% off: He says markets typically undercut support first.

questions.q: Which setup's trigger is this?
questions.story: A leader flushes 2.4 ATR on heavy volume. Two sessions later it undercuts the flush low and closes back above it. You buy the reclaim.
questions.why: Capitulation. It is bought on the undercut and reclaim of the flush low within 3 sessions. A parabolic long is bought that day on the VWAP reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: Count the sessions. The reclaim after the flush is Capitulation.

wrong.Parabolic Long; the VWAP reclaim: A parabolic long is bought the same day on the VWAP reclaim.
wrong.Mean Reversion; the 50-day: The story gives an undercut and reclaim of a flush low. That is this setup's trigger.
wrong.Oops Reversal; the gap: An Oops gaps under the prior day's low in an orderly pullback.

questions.q: Capitulation, or something milder?
choices: Milder; it is far short of 15%
questions.story: A leader drops 6% in one day into its 50-day on heavy volume. It is 7% off its 10-day high.
questions.answer: Milder; it is far short of 15%
questions.why: Milder. A capitulation needs a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume and 15% or more off the 10-session high. A one-day drop into a level is a leader flush, not this.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stretch. 7% is a pullback.

wrong.Capitulation; heavy volume is enough: Volume is one gate. The stretch is another, and 7% is short of 15%.
wrong.Capitulation; it hit its 50-day: Touching the 50-day is a pullback. The stretch is far short.
wrong.Parabolic Long; it fell 6%: A parabolic long is a burst of days, not a one-day drop.

questions.q: Capitulation, or something else?
choices: An undercut and rally, not a flush
A capitulation; it undercut a level
questions.story: A stock dips 1% under a visible level in an ordinary pullback. Its 50-day is not falling and volume is light. It closes back above the level.
questions.answer: An undercut and rally, not a flush
questions.why: An undercut and rally. It undercuts a visible level after an ordinary dip and needs no volume. A capitulation reclaims its own flush low after a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume.
questions.lesson_line: A small dip and a reclaim is a U&R. A flush is bigger.

wrong.A capitulation; it undercut a level: A capitulation needs a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume, not a 1% dip.
wrong.A parabolic long: There is no burst down here.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: An Oops Reversal, not a capitulation
questions.story: A stock gaps under yesterday's low in an orderly pullback and reclaims it the same day on a narrow range.
questions.answer: An Oops Reversal, not a capitulation
questions.why: An Oops Reversal. It gaps under the prior day's low in an orderly pullback. A capitulation flush is 2 ATR or more on 2x volume at the end of a 15% fall.
questions.lesson_line: Orderly pullback and a narrow range is an Oops, not a flush.

wrong.A capitulation; it gapped down: A capitulation flush is 2 ATR or more on 2x volume, at the end of a 15% fall.
wrong.A Wyckoff spring: A spring needs a flat range behind it. This is an orderly pullback.
wrong.A parabolic long: There is no burst down before it.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: A Wyckoff spring; there is a range
A capitulation; it dipped under a level
questions.story: A stock sits in a flat 30-session range. It dips under the floor and closes back inside.
questions.answer: A Wyckoff spring; there is a range
questions.why: A Wyckoff spring. There is a flat range behind the dip. A capitulation has no range behind it; it is a straight fall.
questions.lesson_line: A range behind the dip is a spring. A straight fall is a capitulation.

wrong.A capitulation; it dipped under a level: A capitulation is a straight fall with no range behind it.
wrong.A parabolic long: A parabolic long is a burst down, not a dip from a range.

questions.q: Capitulation, or something else?
choices: A capitulation; it hit the 20 EMA
questions.story: A leader drifts six sessions on light volume to its rising 20 EMA and bounces.
questions.why: A moving-average pullback. A capitulation falls through the 5, 9 and 20-day on 2x volume with a 2 ATR flush bar. This drift was quiet.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet drift to a rising average is a pullback.

wrong.A capitulation; it hit the 20 EMA: A capitulation falls through the short averages on heavy volume.
wrong.A parabolic long: A parabolic long is a burst down. This was a quiet drift.
wrong.An Oops Reversal: An Oops gaps under the prior day's low. This stock drifted.

questions.q: Is this a capitulation long?
choices: Yes, if it gaps down tomorrow
questions.story: A stock falls 40% in three days after the company admits accounting fraud. Volume is huge.
questions.why: No. A real business break, where the selling is informed, is not this setup. Panic selling is forced. This selling has a reason.
questions.lesson_line: Informed selling is not a capitulation.

wrong.Yes; the volume is huge: Huge volume shows selling, not whether it is forced or informed.
wrong.Yes; 40% is a deep flush: Depth is not the test. The reason for the selling is.
wrong.Yes, if it gaps down tomorrow: A gap down does not turn informed selling into a panic.

questions.q: What does the index tell you?
choices: The crash may have another leg
questions.story: You bought a leader's reclaim after a 16.5% flush. The same week the index makes a new low.
questions.answer: The crash may have another leg
questions.why: The crash may have another leg. BN was stopped on day 1 and later traded 41% under the buy as the index made a new low.
questions.lesson_line: A new index low while you hold is a warning.

wrong.The stop can be removed: The stop is the exit. It stays.
wrong.The bounce is confirmed: A new index low says the opposite.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Log it; a new buy needs a new trigger
questions.story: You bought the reclaim at 64.66 with a stop at 63.75. Next day trades 23 cents under the stop, stops you out, then closes near its high.
questions.answer: Log it; a new buy needs a new trigger
questions.why: Log it. The stop was right by the rule and the trade still lost. After a stop-out a new buy needs the setup to trigger again, as a new trade.
questions.lesson_line: A right stop can still lose. Take it and wait for a new trigger.

wrong.Buy back at once, bigger: A new buy needs a new trigger, not a bigger size.
wrong.Move the old stop lower: The stop was the exit. It is already used.
wrong.Blame the setup and quit: A planned loss is the cost of the trade, not proof the setup is broken.

questions.q: What is the warning sign?
choices: A late reclaim, sector still breaking
questions.story: The flush was on a Friday. The reclaim only came on the third session, and the sector is still breaking.
questions.answer: A late reclaim, sector still breaking
questions.why: A late reclaim in a sector still breaking. COP reclaimed on the third session, the next session traded through the stop, and the stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: A late reclaim in a breaking group is a warning.

wrong.The volume was too high: Heavy volume is wanted in a flush.
wrong.The stop was too wide: COP's stop was 1.52%, which is tight.
wrong.The flush was too deep: Depth is not the problem. The late reclaim and the sector are.

questions.q: With a typical stop of 1.7%, about how big a bounce is 3R?
questions.why: About 5%. Three times a 1.7% risk is about 5%, and 5R is about 9%. These are short bounces, not trend trades.
questions.lesson_line: Tight stops mean short targets. 3R is about a 5% bounce.

wrong.About 1.7%: That is one R, not three.
wrong.About 17%: That would be ten times the risk. 3R is about 5%.
wrong.About 50%: That is far beyond 3R. The median stop is 1.7%.

questions.q: In our scan of 2,220 reclaims, about what share reached 3R before the stop?
questions.why: About half: 52.3% reached 3R and 43.1% reached 5R before the stop. That is a fixed stop with no trims.
questions.lesson_line: About half got to 3R. The stop and trims do the rest.

wrong.About nine in ten: 52.3% reached 3R, and 81% were stopped at some point.

questions.q: 81% were stopped at some point, yet 52.3% reached 3R. Why?
choices: The fixed stop never moves; fades return
The scan used a wide stop
The scan only kept the winners
questions.answer: The fixed stop never moves; fades return
questions.why: The stop never moves in the scan, so the fade after the bounce usually comes back to it. That is why we trim at 3R and move to breakeven.
questions.lesson_line: Bounces fade. Trim, then protect the rest.

wrong.The scan used a wide stop: The median stop was tight, about 1.7%.
wrong.3R is a bad target: 52.3% reached it. The point is what happens after.
wrong.The scan only kept the winners: The scan counted all 2,220 reclaims that passed its rules.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: After a three-day flush the low is 38.48. A leader trades down to 38.31, then back above 38.48 and closes higher. You buy the reclaim at 38.49.
questions.why: Market at the reclaim, 38.49; stop a few cents under the undercut low, 38.26; a third at 3R. ALB reached 22.5R at best.
questions.lesson_line: Write the plan before the buy.

wrong.Limit 39.23; stop 38.31; all at 5R: A stop exactly on the low is not a few cents under it, and we sell a third at 3R.
wrong.Market 38.31; stop 37.00; hold a month: 38.31 is the undercut price, not the reclaim, and a month is not this trade.

questions.q: What is the trade?
choices: Buy the Monday reclaim of the flush low
questions.story: Thursday and Friday flush a leader 23% on 2.28x volume. Monday it opens under the flush low, undercuts it and closes above it.
questions.answer: Buy the Monday reclaim of the flush low
questions.why: Buy the Monday reclaim of the flush low. OKTA opened 88.34 under the flush low, undercut 87.93 and closed 91.24.
questions.lesson_line: Several down days, then a Monday gap and reclaim.

wrong.Buy the Friday close: That is the knife. Nearly half of flush closes are undercut.
wrong.Short the Monday gap: The Monday closed above the flush low. That is the turn, not a short.
wrong.Wait two weeks: The reclaim is the trigger, and it came on Monday.

questions.q: Hidden ticker; the chart ends on a flush day on heavy volume. Watch it for a reclaim, or pass?
choices: Watch it; a fast flush into a level
Pass; a slow grind with no burst
Pass; the volume is under the average
questions.answer: Watch it; a fast flush into a level
questions.why: Watch it. A 2.41 ATR flush on 2.25x volume, 20.8% under the 10-day high close, into the round number 100 and the 200-day. The next day it undercut and closed 6% higher.
questions.lesson_line: A fast flush into a real level is worth watching.

wrong.Pass; a slow grind with no burst: Look again: three lower closes ending in a 2.41 ATR bar.
wrong.Pass; the volume is under the average: The flush day ran 2.25 times its average volume.

questions.q: Hidden ticker; a flush day: 2.95 ATR, 2.23x volume, the low 12.9% under the 10-day high close. Watch it, or pass?
choices: Pass; only a pullback in a leader
Watch it; the volume is heavy
questions.answer: Pass; only a pullback in a leader
questions.why: Pass. The low was only 12.9% under the 10-day high close and the stretch needs 15%. It was a 13% dip to the rising 50-day in a leader.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy volume and a deep ATR still need the 15% stretch.

wrong.Watch it; the volume is heavy: The volume clears 2x, but the stretch is short of 15%.
wrong.Watch it; 2.95 ATR is deep: The ATR clears 2, but the stretch is short of 15%.
